interview.question: How would you pick Axle's first market outside GB?
answer: Score markets on rules, device base and route to revenue, like my Cornwall Insight due diligence.
Check market access first: balancing rules, aggregator rights and supplier partners, as I did at NESO.
Start with a pilot with one supplier or grid operator to test revenue per device.

learn.title: How Axle makes money
bullets: Axle controls home devices so they use power when it is cheap and green.
It earns from flexibility markets, grid services and supplier savings on energy cost.
Revenue is shared across many devices, so revenue per device drives the business case.
learn.so_what: You can frame every country choice as expected revenue per device against the cost of entry.

moves.text: Read the Electrek story on GM's V2G pilot; draft a two-line LinkedIn comment with your flexibility view.
Skim the Dutch grid congestion story; note how Enexis (Dutch network operator) buys flexibility for later interview use.
Follow E.ON on LinkedIn; note how its bidirectional pilots could shape supplier partnerships.

takeaways.text: GM is paying US drivers for car-to-grid power, so home flexibility is going mainstream.
E.ON is piloting two-way EV charging in Czechia, so suppliers are a likely Axle partner type.
Enexis and Siemens target Dutch congestion, so the Netherlands is a likely early Axle market.

top3.headline: GM launches California V2G pilot
bullets: GM Energy and WeaveGrid pilot with Southern California Edison customers.
Drivers could get over $16,000 towards equipment and installation.
top3.why: Carmakers and utilities are now paying for vehicle-to-grid, a new route to market for flexibility.
top3.use: Cite this in interviews as proof home flexibility is going mainstream in the US.

top3.headline: E.ON pilots two-way EV charging in Czechia
bullets: E.ON is testing bidirectional EV charging in the Czech Republic.
It is a pilot, not yet a commercial rollout.
top3.why: Large suppliers are testing vehicle-to-grid, which makes them likely Axle partners.
top3.use: Follow E.ON's flexibility team on LinkedIn; they are a likely Axle partner.

top3.headline: Siemens and Enexis tackle Dutch congestion
bullets: Siemens and Enexis are teaming up on Dutch grid congestion.
Enexis is a Dutch distribution network operator.
top3.why: Dutch network operators need flexibility, which opens partnership routes for Axle.
top3.use: Add Enexis to your list of grid operator targets for the Netherlands.

top3.headline: SP Energy Networks North West launches day-ahead flexibility
bullets: SP Electricity North West has launched day-ahead flexibility markets.
This adds a new short-notice market in GB distribution.
top3.why: New GB distribution flexibility markets give Axle more revenue routes at home.
top3.use: Mention this in interviews as a GB revenue stream you track.

top3.headline: Germany advances over 4GWh of batteries
bullets: Elements Green, EnBW, Flower and others progress projects towards construction.
Total is over 4GWh ahead of a year-end FID deadline.
top3.why: Fast grid battery growth means tougher price competition for home flexibility in Germany.
top3.use: Note this as a risk in any Germany entry case you discuss.
